Voting has ended in Israel.
Initial exit polls suggest most Israelis have voted against Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

Exit polls have found Gadi Eisenkot, the former military chief, in the lead with his center-right

The U.S. has not yet recognized the results of elections in Brazil this week, but it is
welcoming the man who lost right-wing Trump ally Flavio Bolsonaro, as NPR's Michelle Kellerman
reports.
The State Department says it will issue visas to Flavio Bolsonaro and his family and allow
them entry into the United States.
Bolsonaro lost a run-off election to his left-wing rival, Luis Inacio Lula da Silva.
A day later, a Brazilian Supreme Court justice ordered him to hand in his passports as part
of an investigation into alleged money laundering charges Bolsonaro denies.
Like Bolsonaro, President Trump has suggested the vote was rigged, though neither provided
evidence of that.
Bolsonaro's father, former President Jair Bolsonaro, remains under house arrest after
being convicted of attempting a coup following his 2022 election loss.
Michelle Kellerman, NPR News, the State Department.
Another top official at the CDC is leaving the agency, and PR's Rob Stein has the story.
Dr. Jennifer Shuford is stepping down as the CDC's chief medical officer and deputy director
after six months on the job.
Shuford says she's leaving to spend more time with her family.
The departure is just the latest upheaval at the nation's premier public health agency,
which has been rocked by mass firings, budget cuts, leadership turmoil, and charges of political
interference by Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr.
All this comes as the CDC has been largely silent on the role of vaccination in fighting
the worst U.S. measles outbreak in decades.
Rob Stein, NPR News.

regulation.
Democratic-led cities had sought to revive the rule, which allowed immigration judges
to pause some deportation proceedings.
They argued it helped crime victims and vulnerable juveniles, Texas and the Trump administration
had blocked the regulation.
This is NPR.
Russia and Ukraine have begun a localized ceasefire in a Southern Ukrainian city to
allow a humanitarian mission.
The truce, brokered by First Lady Melania Trump, aims to allow the delivery of aid later
this week to the city of Olesky, where supplies have run dangerously low.
Despite the ceasefire, Russia continues missile attacks on other cities.
The Ebola case count in the Democratic Republic of Congo is now over 10,000, as NPR's Jonathan
Lambert reports about half of those cases have died.
The DRC reached this grim threshold in just over five months.
For context, at this point, in the largest Ebola outbreak ever, the 2014 West Africa
outbreak, only about 4,000 people were infected.
That trajectory makes this current outbreak the fastest spreading ever.
A number of factors have fueled this rapid spread.
For one, the virus was spreading undetected for months before officials declared the outbreak.
It's also spreading in remote parts of DRC, making the response harder.
Officials have made some progress in containing it.
Better testing, treatment and outreach have helped rein in cases in areas where the outbreak
started.
But the virus is ramping up in new parts of DRC, so case counts continue climbing.
In recent weeks, that uncontrolled spread has spilled into neighboring countries, including
Kenya and Nigeria.
Jonathan Lambert, NPR News.
